thread:
alex: Quick q — who actually 'owns' timeouts in our SDKs? Should clients set a hard per-request timeout or should the app/service layer do it? I see node/py/go behave differently and it causes confusion with server-side 30s LB kills :thinking:

maria: I think ownership should be split. SDKs should provide reasonable defaults to avoid footguns (hung streams, leaked sockets) but not silently swallow app-level timeouts. Docs + clear opt-outs are key. Also call out infra limits (LB kills). @alex

sean: Follow-up: retries complicate this. If SDK retries under the hood and also enforces a long timeout, apps may never see a 504 and retry loops can amplify load. We need rules: if retrying, shorter per-attempt timeout + overall cap.

lina: Node example pattern we ship in examples (uses AbortController):
```js
const ac = new AbortController();
const timeout = setTimeout(() => ac.abort(), 45_000); // per-request cap
try {
  const res = await client.generate({ prompt }, { signal: ac.signal });
} finally {
  clearTimeout(timeout);
}
```
This lets app control cancellation and still uses builtin abort semantics.

ci-bot: Perf note: load tests show our ingress LB kills connections at ~60s for long-polling routes. Also p95 token latency ~600ms. Worth documenting so SDK defaults don't conflict.

maria: Proposal (SDK design): three-layer timeout model —
- connect/init timeout (short, e.g., 5s)
- per-attempt/request timeout (defaultable, e.g., 30–60s)
- overall operation cap for retries (opt-in or explicit, e.g., 120s)
Expose explicit params: requestTimeout, streamingKeepalive, abortSignal. Defaults should be conservative but overridable.

alex: How do we map this across languages? Node has AbortController; Go uses context; Python has asyncio/timeouts. Quick mapping examples please.

sean: Go example:
```go
ctx, cancel := context.WithTimeout(ctx, 45*time.Second)
defer cancel()
resp, err := client.Generate(ctx, req)
```
Python (asyncio) example:
```py
import asyncio
try:
    async with asyncio.timeout(45):
        await client.generate(prompt)
except asyncio.TimeoutError:
    # handle cancellation
```
These keep semantics parallel: SDK should accept context/timeout/signal and not add hidden extra timeouts.

lina: Action: I'll draft an SDK timeout/abort section in the devex SDK design doc with code snippets for node/go/py and heuristics for retries. I'll open a PR and tag @maria @sean for review.

alex: Awesome — thanks Lina. Adding: recommend default per-attempt = 60s, overall cap = none (no silent hard kill) but we log warnings when we hit platform kills so apps can opt-in to an overall cap. :thumbsup:

maria: +1. Also add a short migration note for existing clients that relied on implicit client-level timeouts.

alex: Thanks everyone! :heart:
